summary: Marks the largest aggressive orders from public crypto exchange trades with bubbles, buyers above and sellers below, with absorption and swept levels.
overview: Big Trades marks only the orders that stand out. Each marker is a buy (green) or sell (red) bubble placed at the order's average price. Bigger and brighter markers mean higher impact. Hover or tap a marker for its details.
When a big order came and price did not follow it, the marker is a hollow ring with an A for absorption. The price range an order swept can also be shown.
how: Consecutive same-side fills within a short burst (150 ms gap, up to 4 ticks of price walk) are joined into one parent order with its total size and average price. Optionally, same-side orders at one price can be summed over a time window, so a big resting order filled by many small ones shows as one marker.

In Automatic mode the size threshold is set so that about 15 markers show per 6.5-hour session at Medium intensity (40, 25 or 8 at Very low, Low and Strong). Manual mode uses your own min and max size. Impact combines size against normal, levels swept, and what price did in the next 60 seconds. Absorption means price moved 0.2 ATR or less in the order's direction. Order flow comes from public exchange trades for crypto.
use: Some traders watch where large orders appeared near highs, lows or key levels.
Use the absorption marks to see big orders that price did not follow.
Some traders run two copies with different size bands to separate sizes.
Use the hover card to read each order's size and fills.
notes: On futures charts use Big Trades (L2); a saved futures chart that still holds this one is switched to it automatically. Crypto charts keep this one.
Needs per-trade data; other symbols show a note.
Joining fills into one order is an estimate based on timing and price.
